plan: implement Noble Family variand of Love Letter

turns.question: Where does the card-type rank live in this engine, and what does adding a card type touch?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Rank is the CardType enum index itself; adding a type touches the enum, sprite frame index (cards.png has 9 frames of 11x17), card_count/card_names, find_valid_moves, resolve_effect, eval_moves, type_selector.tscn, and help pages.
turns.userAnswer: Discovered: Deck.CardType (deck.gd:4-13) doubles as the rank table — round_over picks the highest enum int, Baron compares my_type > their_type, eval_moves scores with GOOD * _target_type and mem > Handmaid; Card.gd sets _sprite.frame = type against a 99x17 sheet (9 frames, 11x17 each); find_valid_moves guesses range(Priest, Unknown); countess_restricted hardcodes Prince/King as "men"; eval_moves has no default branch, so an unhandled type scores LOSE=0 and level 4 degrades to uniform random; main.gd:284 asserts exactly 1 card in hand for every active seat.
turns.notes: Constrains every later answer: any new card must land in rank order in the enum, and the 1-card hand invariant decides which Noble Family effects are cheap.

turns.question: Which family-dealing table do we implement, given the doc's 'exactly 4 cards remain' contradicts its own per-player numbers?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Doc per-player numbers: 1 to each, then 5 more (2p) / 4 more (3p) / 3 more (4p) -> family 5/4/3, burn 3/1/0, deck left 1/0/0; the 'exactly 4 remain' headline is arithmetically impossible with those numbers.
turns.userAnswer: Doc per-player numbers (family 5/4/3, burn 3/1/0, deck 1/0/0)
turns.notes: Combined with the engine widow (3/1/1) the real remainders are 0/0/1 in the main pile; widow pile holds the burned cards.

turns.question: Is the card dealt as 'their first hand' counted inside the family, or is the family only the extra distributed cards?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Family excludes the first hand (family 5/4/3, total owned 6/5/4), so the family pile is exactly the drawable set.
turns.userAnswer: First card is dealt to each player's hand. Then everyone receives noble family cards that they will draw from (family pile = drawable cards only).
turns.notes: Player starts a round with 1 hand card + family pile of 5/4/3 (2p/3p/4p).

turns.question: Whose hand size do we keep at decision time: draw-then-play or play-then-draw?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Draw from family first, then play 1 of 2 - matches the existing new_turn -> deal_card -> find_valid_moves flow and keeps eval_moves' leftover-card logic valid.
turns.userAnswer: Draw from family first, then play 1 of 2
turns.notes: Hand is 2 cards at decision time; the leftover becomes the active card.

turns.question: How does the Countess restriction work in the variant?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Unchanged: Countess + Prince/King in the 2-card hand forces the Countess play ('No other changes').
turns.userAnswer: Unchanged: Countess + man in hand forces the Countess play
turns.notes: countess_restricted() needs no edit under draw-then-play.

turns.question: What exactly happens when a player is eliminated: reveal hand+family, where do the cards go, and how is deck._left accounting affected?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Reveal hand+family face-up at the seat, cards stay there (not moved to the discard pile), and Main decrements _deck._left for each revealed card (public, out of play).
turns.userAnswer: Reveal, update memories, discard all of them without effects
turns.notes: User answer says the revealed family/hand cards ARE discarded (no effects), which conflicts with the doc's 'They are not considered discarded'; confirm discard animation/target and _left decrement in round 2.

turns.question: Where is the round-end condition checked?
turns.recommendedAnswer: At turn start: seat to act has an empty family -> round_over() (same slot as the current deck-empty check).
turns.userAnswer: At turn start: seat to act has empty family -> round_over()
turns.notes: Single round-end rule; family only shrinks on your own turn.

turns.question: A Prince discards the target's active card; what if the target's family is empty?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Target is eliminated (set_inactive, reveal, no new card) and the round continues; the round-end check stays at turn start.
turns.userAnswer: Draw the widow in this case
turns.notes: Introduces the widow pile as the Prince-redraw fallback in the variant. Need the empty-widow fallback and confirmation that turn-start drawing still comes only from the family.

turns.question: Which burn/widow count does the variant use (doc says burn 1; engine uses widow 3 for 2p, 1 for 3-4p)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Follow the engine's widow counts (3 for 2p, 1 for 3p/4p); matches the doc's '13 remaining' arithmetic for 2p and keeps Deck.prepare() as the burn source.
turns.userAnswer: Engine widow: 3 for 2p, 1 for 3p/4p (doc 'no burn' for 4p ignored)
turns.notes: With families 5/4/3 the main pile ends at 0/0/1 cards for 2/3/4 players.

turns.question: Who can see whose family?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Own family face-up at all times; opponents' families face-down with a visible card count.
turns.userAnswer: Own face-up; opponents' families fully hidden (no count)
turns.notes: No count badge for AI families; family becomes public only via the elimination reveal.

turns.question: How should the human draw-selection interface look in the Main scene?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Modal family panel over the table, built like the TypeSelector overlay, opened when a draw is required, plus a small face-up stack at your seat.
turns.userAnswer: Modal family panel over the table (TypeSelector-style), plus a small face-up stack at your seat
turns.notes: 84x48 viewport has no room for 5-card rows for four seats; reuse the TypeSelector pattern.

turns.question: How is the draw choice represented in the AI's move list?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Joint (draw, play) moves: Move gains the drawn family card, find_valid_moves enumerates family pick x played card x target, eval_moves scores the drawn card as the leftover card.
turns.userAnswer: Joint (draw, play) moves enumerated in find_valid_moves
turns.notes: Exact fit for my_type = hand.get_child(1 - m._played_card_idx).

turns.question: What draw rule do AI levels 1-4 use?
turns.recommendedAnswer: L1 first valid move, L2 uniform random, L3 cheapest play + cheapest draw, L4 full weighted scoring of joint moves.
turns.userAnswer: L1 first, L2 random, L3 cheapest play + cheapest draw, L4 weighted eval
turns.notes: Preserves each level's existing personality.

turns.question: In what order are family cards enumerated (so L1's 'first valid move' is reproducible)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: As-dealt (deck) order, no sorting - no extra state, L1 stays an arbitrary-first-move AI.
turns.userAnswer: As-dealt order (deck order), no sorting
turns.notes: Deterministic under a fixed seed.

turns.question: Should eval_moves gain new scoring terms for the variant?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Minimal: the drawn family card is the leftover card only; no new family-templating heuristics, measure later.
turns.userAnswer: Minimal: drawn family card = leftover card, no new scoring terms
turns.notes: Rebalance (keep best family card for last, family-size terms) is deferred to measurement.

turns.question: How does the Noble Family entry under Play work on the start page?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Tapping PLAY expands the Play row in place into CLASSIC / NOBLE FAMILY sub-rows.
turns.userAnswer: PLAY leads to a new GameMode scene with CLASSIC, NOBLE FAMILY, BACK options
turns.notes: New scene/node (mode selector) shown from PLAY; BACK returns to the start page. Plumbing details to confirm in round 2.

turns.question: Is the selected mode persisted to user://options.cfg?
turns.recommendedAnswer: No: mode resets to Classic on app start / return to menu; explicit choice per game, no config migration.
turns.userAnswer: Not persisted: mode resets to Classic on app start / return to menu
turns.notes: Speedrun and existing config keys stay untouched.

turns.question: Should Noble Family rounds feed the Stats page?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Share the existing totals/wins table - variant rounds count as ordinary rounds, zero data-model change.
turns.userAnswer: Separate per-mode stats with a mode switch on the Stats page
turns.notes: Doubles the counters (24 = 2 modes x 6 levels x 2), needs saved keys per mode, a reset rule, and a mode-switch widget in stats.tscn. Round-2 questions pending.

turns.question: Add rules text for the variant to the existing Help pager?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Add 2-3 Noble Family pages to the existing pager (Setup/Turn/Elimination/Round End variants).
turns.userAnswer: Pages shown only while the variant mode is active
turns.notes: Needs a rule for Help opened from the start page before any mode is chosen and from Pause; round-2 question.

turns.question: What test coverage do we add?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Both: a variant smoke suite (all-AI games at 2/3/4 players, rounds/eliminations flow) and a deterministic scripted fake-deck repro suite (family sizes, draw legality, round-end condition).
turns.userAnswer: Variant smoke suite + deterministic scripted-deck repro suite
turns.notes: Mirrors tests/README.md practice (godot --headless --path . tests/<scene>.tscn, exit code).

turns.question: Exact implementation of the out-of-round reveal: reveal hand+family, where do the cards go, and how does deck._left accounting react?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Reveal face-up, then animate them to the discard pile (no effects) and decrement _deck._left - the doc's 'not discarded' read as 'no discard effect, never in the pile before'.
turns.userAnswer: Reveal face-up, then move to the discard pile and decrement _deck._left, no effects
turns.notes: Resolves the doc conflict explicitly; Main.discard() reused; Level 4's _left stays 'not played and in play'.

turns.question: Scope of the widow-draw fallback and the empty-widow case.
turns.recommendedAnswer: Widow = Prince-redraw fallback only (like deal_card(tp, true)); turn-start draws come only from the family; an empty widow eliminates the Prince target.
turns.userAnswer: Widow = Prince-redraw fallback only; empty widow eliminates the target; turn start is family-only
turns.notes: Round-end condition stays a single check at turn start.

turns.question: How is the widow pile shown in the variant?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Classic Deck.gd behaviour: face-down pile visible while non-empty, no card count (hidden information).
turns.userAnswer: Visible face-down pile, no card count (classic behaviour)
turns.notes: Keeps left_cards_sim.py's hidden-widow finding valid.

turns.question: Where does the new GameMode scene live and how does Main learn the mode?
turns.recommendedAnswer: New GameMode node in application.tscn (hidden by default, like LevelSelector/Stats/Pause); PLAY shows it, BACK returns to Start; application.gd sets Main.noble_family before init_players, exactly like it assigns ai_level today.
turns.userAnswer: New GameMode node in application.tscn; application.gd sets Main.noble_family before init_players
turns.notes: No autoload/singleton; Start.play_pressed now opens the mode selector instead of starting a game.

turns.question: Does speed_run / the headless export flags reach the variant?
turns.recommendedAnswer: No: speed_run stays classic-only; variant tests instantiate Main directly and set the noble_family flag (tests/smoke_games.gd pattern).
turns.userAnswer: speed_run stays classic; variant only from the menu and from tests
turns.notes: Existing measured speedrun numbers are untouched.

turns.question: Family data model: where do family cards live?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Plain Array[Deck.CardType] per seat (dealt by Deck, flow owned by Main); Card nodes materialized only for the human's stack and the modal; AI draws instantiate the card in AnimationLayer and slide it from the seat.
turns.userAnswer: Type arrays per seat; Card nodes only for the human's stack/modal
turns.notes: AI never gets Card nodes for family; Main keeps state changes central (design.md guideline).

turns.question: Where does the human's face-up family stack sit, given the 84x48 geometry?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Cascading face-up row in seat 0's free bottom strip (x5..52, y31..48), rank corners visible; AI families are hidden so the top seats need nothing.
turns.userAnswer: Cascading face-up row in seat 0's free bottom strip (all ranks readable)
turns.notes: Only seat 0 has a face-up stack; top seats collide with Marker0's played-card area.

turns.question: How is 'you may look at your noble family at any time' honoured for the human?
turns.recommendedAnswer: The always face-up cascade stack is enough; the modal opens only when a draw is required.
turns.userAnswer: The always face-up stack is enough; the modal opens only when a draw is required
turns.notes: No browse mode, no extra button.

turns.question: How should the 10-12 family cards be dealt on screen each round?
turns.recommendedAnswer: First-hand card animated normally; family cards appear instantly in the stack with a single deal sound.
turns.userAnswer: First hand animated; family cards appear instantly
turns.notes: Keeps round setup under ~1s on mobile.

turns.question: What does Deck.gd show in the variant (main pile ends at 1/0/? cards)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Hide the main pile sprite in the variant, keep the widow pile visible as the Prince fallback.
turns.userAnswer: Hide main pile in the variant; show the widow pile
turns.notes: Avoids a misleading 1-card pile in some counts.

turns.question: Per-mode Stats: what is the switch mechanism and data layout?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Left/right digit-button tabs (SpeedLevel pattern) flipping one 6-row table between Classic and Noble Family; tab defaults to the mode just played; saved as two ConfigFile keys, 12 counters each.
turns.userAnswer: Left/right tab buttons over one table; per-mode keys in options.cfg
turns.notes: Doubled table (24 chars/line) does not fit 84px; digit_button.tscn is reused.

turns.question: What does the Stats Reset button clear with per-mode tables?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Only the visible mode's table; the stale-data drop check in load_config() moves to a per-table size check.
turns.userAnswer: Reset clears only the currently visible mode's table
turns.notes: Tab-local reset.

turns.question: Variant-only Help pages: what shows where, given Help is reachable from Start (no mode chosen) and from Pause (mode known)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Append variant pages tagged variant_only; hidden on the Start page, shown in Pause during a variant game.
turns.userAnswer: variant_only pages appended; hidden on the Start page, shown in Pause during a variant game
turns.notes: Existing pages stay untouched.

turns.question: What belongs in _deck._left in the variant (Level 4's Guard/Prince counting reads it)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Everything not yet played and in play: deck leftovers + widow + every live seat's family; decrement on play and on elimination reveal; family draws do not change it.
turns.userAnswer: Deck leftovers + widow + all live families (decrement on play and on elimination reveal)
turns.notes: Keeps P(target holds t) = _left[t]/sum(_left) valid; family cards are hidden info, not out of play.

turns.question: How is the 4-player deal resolved (4 first-hand + 3 family each needs 16 cards, so the engine's 1-card widow burn cannot coexist with 3-card families)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: 4p burns nothing (the doc's own 'do not burn' line): families 3 each, main pile empty, no widow pile in 4p, so a Prince target with an empty family in 4p is eliminated; 2p/3p keep the widow fallback.
turns.userAnswer: 4p: burn 0, families 3 each, no widow pile in 4p
turns.notes: Final deal table (16 cards): burn 3/1/0, first hand 1/1/1, family 5/4/3, main pile left 1/0/0, widow pile 3/1/0 for 2p/3p/4p.

turns.question: What happens when a forced family draw lands on the human mid-effect (his own Prince)?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Open the draw modal at that moment and let the human pick - one interface for every human draw.
turns.userAnswer: The draw modal opens at that moment and the human picks
turns.notes: The modal is the only human draw interface; no auto-draw, no move suppression.

turns.question: Are families re-dealt every round or kept for the whole game?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Re-deal every round from a fresh shuffle (matches _new_round() -> Deck.prepare(); scores persist, families do not).
turns.userAnswer: Re-deal families every round (fresh shuffle)
turns.notes: No family persistence across rounds.

turns.question: How many variant_only Help pages and what do they say?
turns.recommendedAnswer: 4 short pages reusing card_help_page.tscn (show_card = false): Family Setup (burn + 5/4/3 deal), Family Turn (draw from family, widow for Prince only), Family Out (reveal everything, cards leave play), Family Round End (round ends when the seat to act cannot draw).
turns.userAnswer: 4 pages: Setup / Turn / Out / Round End
turns.notes: Text must state the resolved deal table and the widow-fallback rule.

turns.question: Draw modal placement and flow?
turns.recommendedAnswer: TypeSelector pattern: modal Node2D at z_index 10 centered over the Table, family cards in one row with the selection sprite; tap = animate to hand and close; no cancel button because the draw is mandatory.
turns.userAnswer: Centered over the table, tap to draw, no cancel button
turns.notes: Opened at turn start and at mid-effect forced draws.

turns.question: How are the resolved rules documented?
turns.recommendedAnswer: New docs/noble-family-implementation.md (deal table, flow, find_valid_moves/eval_moves extension, stats/help/menu plumbing, test commands); docs/Noble family variant.md stays the untouched source spec.
turns.userAnswer: New docs/noble-family-implementation.md; source spec stays pristine
turns.notes: The two spec contradictions are recorded in the implementation doc, not by editing the spec.
